title: Vikramaditya II Spares Kanchi's Shrines
subtitle: When the Victor Chose Restraint at Kanchi
era: Late Badami Chalukya campaigns, c. 731-740 CE
region: Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu, and Pattadakal, Karnataka
moral: Strength is noblest when it chooses restraint.

sources.citation: Kailasanatha temple pillar inscription, Kanchipuram, South Indian Inscriptions Vol. I, No. 82
sources.note: In-situ primary evidence for Vikramaditya II's conduct at Kanchi.

sources.citation: Kauthem Copper Plates of Vikramaditya II, Epigraphia Indica Vol. XVIII
sources.note: Primary Chalukya grant connected with the Pallava campaign period.

sources.citation: George Michell, Pattadakal, Oxford University Press / ASI (1997)
sources.note: Context for how the Kanchi campaigns shaped Pattadakal architecture.

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a crowned king before distant temple towers

dialogue.text: In the age of Badami’s Chalukyas, Vikramaditya II rode to Kanchi and carved his glory not in ruin, but in restraint.

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over Deccan plateau with distant city

dialogue.text: From the red cliffs of Badami, the Chalukya kings watched the south, where Pallava Kanchi shone like a rival sun.

panels.shot: medium interior shot in royal hall, slight low angle

dialogue.text: Decades earlier, Pulakeshin II had fallen to the Pallavas. The wound lingered; a son must answer where a father had failed.

panels.shot: close-up on Vikramaditya II’s face over the maps

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: We ride not for rage alone, but for memory and measure.

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of marching army on dusty road

dialogue.text: Between c. 731 and 740, his armies pressed south thrice, crossing rivers and ridges toward the famed city of Kanchi.

panels.shot: medium shot at a river crossing, side angle

dialogue.text: The Kauthem copper plates remember these marches, grants of land forged in the shadow of war.

panels.shot: wide shot of Kanchipuram skyline from a distance

dialogue.text: Kanchi, seat of the Pallavas, was more than a fortress. It was a city of stone hymns, of scholars and shrines.

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide at city gate, frontal angle

dialogue.text: The Pallava power bent before him. Victory opened the gates, and with them, the peril of pride.

panels.shot: interior wide of Kailasanatha temple courtyard

dialogue.text: In the Kailasanatha temple, a Pallava jewel of stone, the conqueror entered as a guest beneath another king’s artistry.

panels.shot: close-up on sculpted wall with Vikramaditya II in profile

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: Steel can break stone, but it cannot carve like this.

panels.shot: medium shot of Vikramaditya II addressing officers inside temple

dialogue.text: Here, where a lesser man might boast in ashes, he set a different command.

panels.shot: tight medium on Vikramaditya II, slight low angle

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_ii
dialogue.text: Let no shrine be harmed, no image carried away. Our fame needs no theft.

panels.shot: close-up on a stone pillar being inscribed

dialogue.text: On a pillar of Kailasanatha, his men cut words instead of wounds, an inscription of victory without desecration.

panels.shot: extreme close-up of inscription line with shadowed profile

dialogue.text: It declared that the Chalukya had entered, triumphed, and yet had not seized the temples’ wealth nor scarred their walls.

panels.shot: wide shot of city street with temples intact

dialogue.text: Kanchi did not fall into ruin. Its towers still caught the sun; its lanes still hummed, though under a stranger’s gaze.

panels.shot: medium shot of Vikramaditya II taking leave of Kanchi

dialogue.text: He did not make Kanchi his seat. The city remained Pallava at heart, yet now carried a Chalukya’s memory on its stone.

panels.shot: epic wide of Pattadakal temple complex under construction

dialogue.text: Back in the Deccan, at Pattadakal, new shrines rose. Scholars see in their forms the echo of Kanchi, victory translated into stone.

panels.shot: close-up on sculptor and Vikramaditya II observing a relief

dialogue.text: Stones remember exchanges that chronicles forget. Influence traveled with armies, not only as spoil, but as inspiration.

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Vikramaditya II against sky and temple silhouettes

dialogue.text: Vikramaditya II’s boast at Kanchi was rare: that he spared. In an age of conquest, his name endures where the victor chose to leave another’s gods unbroken.
